C0700.d: No public record shows a carmaker using C0700; public J2012 lists, NHTSA bulletins and maker indexes are silent. The title concerns superimposed steering such as the system from the Bosch-ZF venture that BMW introduced on the 2004 5 Series.
s: Steering warning in the instrument cluster
Steering ratio stays fixed, more wheel turns when parking
c: Damaged bus wiring or connector to the active steering controller
Steering angle or wheel speed message missing from another module
Active steering controller without power or defective

C0710.d: C0710 does not appear in the publicly available J2012 lists, yet GM uses it widely in the brake control module for the steering angle it feeds to stability control. Saab 9-5 2011 wording matches the title for subcode 00 and adds 42 (centering not stored) and 5A (signal missing, offset out of range or at odds with yaw rate); the 9-4X adds 71 for invalid data.
s: Service StabiliTrak or stability message, ESC indicator on
Unwanted stability intervention while cornering
c: Steering angle sensor not centred after alignment or repair
Steering wheel mis-splined, or suspension, wheelbase or tyres changed
Faulty steering angle sensor, connector or worn column bearing
Brake module programmed for the wrong sensor design

C0712.d: No carmaker is known to document C0712; it is not in the J2012 tables, bulletins or maker indexes searched. The title points to a position input of the power steering whose value is outside the expected band or does not track the other signals.
s: Power steering warning, assist reduced or lost
Steering wheel off centre or vehicle drifts to one side
c: Steering angle or position learn skipped or done wrongly
Position sensor in the steering gear or column defective
Intermittent connection in the sensor wiring

C0715.d: C0715 is not traceable in public material; the publicly available J2012 tables, the NHTSA bulletin index and maker code lists all lack it. The function it names is well known from engine diagnostics, where the same check runs as P0551.
s: Idle dips or engine stalls at full steering lock
Idle stays raised while driving straight
c: Pressure sensor or switch stuck or drifting
Fluid seeping into the sensor connector
Pump pressure abnormal due to low fluid or worn pump

C0720.d: No publicly available J2012 list contains C0720, and the only maker that uses it means something else: GM files C0720 71 on the 2011 Saab 9-5 and 9-4X as invalid engine torque data received by the suspension module over CAN; the damping control stays off for that ignition cycle and a history entry clears after 41 fault-free cycles. For the torque sensor in the title, GM uses C0545 instead (bulletin PIT5213B for 2014-
s: Sudden loss of steering assist with warning message and chime
Heavy steering at low speed
c: Loose or corroded connector between sensor and EPS module
Sensor zero point not learned after replacement

C0725.d: C0725 has no public documentation; the publicly available J2012 tables, NHTSA bulletins and maker indexes leave it out. Carmakers file assist motor faults elsewhere: GM uses C0475, including symptom 64 for a detected slip in the motor circuit (bulletin PIT5213B), and Stellantis C1592, which the 2019 Jeep Cherokee could log as a general electrical failure and which a software flash addressed under bulletin 08-034-20,
s: Steering warning, assist reduced or lost
Steering feels notchy or jerks while turning
c: Motor winding or power stage in the EPS unit defective
Module software misdiagnoses the motor circuit (update available)
Poor connection between module and motor

C0727.d: C0727 has no public trace in the public J2012 tables, NHTSA bulletins or maker indexes, and trailer faults usually sit in B or U codes. The circuits behind the title are documented.
s: Trailer lamps inoperative or flickering
Trailer connected/disconnected message without reason
c: Moisture or corrosion in the vehicle trailer socket
Short, LED load too low or own lighting module on the trailer
Damaged vehicle harness or trailer lighting module

C0730.d: Neither the publicly available J2012 lists nor NHTSA bulletins or maker indexes show C0730, so its use is not publicly verifiable. The sensor it names reports the rotor angle of the brushless assist motor, without which the module cannot commutate the phases or run field-oriented current control.
s: Steering assist drops out suddenly, warning lamp on
Steering jerky or uneven while turning
c: Rotor position sensor in the EPS motor defective
Poor connection between sensor and control board
Sensor magnet loose or misaligned after repair

C0735.d: No known public source uses C0735; it is absent from the published J2012 lists, from NHTSA bulletins and from maker indexes. Carmakers report an internal EPS controller fault under other codes.
s: Service power steering message, steering lamp on
Assist reduced or absent from start-up
c: Module software fault, cleared by reprogramming
Internal hardware failure of the EPS controller
Wrong steering gear or module installed, setup not completed

C0740.d: C0740 is not publicly documented by any carmaker; publicly available J2012 lists, NHTSA bulletins and maker indexes do not contain it. The title concerns the heavy supply feed of an electric steering, which draws high currents when the wheel is turned at standstill.
s: Assist weakens or cuts out at low speed and full lock
Steering wheel jerks, other displays flicker
c: Loose or corroded main power or ground connection at the rack
Discharged or failing battery, high-resistance battery cables
Battery cable shorting elsewhere or poor body ground

C0745.d: Public documentation of C0745 is missing; it is not in the publicly available J2012 tables, in NHTSA bulletins or in maker indexes. GM reports an overheated EPS controller as C0176 (PIT5213B).
s: Steering gradually heavier after repeated manoeuvring
Power steering warning message
c: Long parking manoeuvres or holding the wheel at full lock
Stiff steering gear, joints or tyres raising motor load
Temperature estimate or sensor in the module faulty

C0750.d: None of the public code lists carries C0750. GM, however, uses it in its tire pressure monitoring for the left front wheel transmitter, and the Saab 9-5 (2010-2011) and 9-4X service pages define the subcodes: 03 for a weak sensor battery, 29 for a sensor that sends too few telegrams, 39 for an internal sensor defect.
s: TPMS lamp flashes about one minute after start, then stays on
Dashes instead of a pressure value for the left front tire
Service tire monitor message in the driver display
c: Built-in battery of the wheel sensor exhausted (subcode 03)
Sensor damaged during tire service, after a flat or replaced by a valve without sensor
Radio interference from aftermarket devices or metallised window tint (GM PIC5650M)
Remote receiver or its antenna unplugged or faulty

C0784.d: Searches for C0784 came up empty: the public code lists, the NHTSA bulletin index, GM's keyword table and the Saab and Mitsubishi indexes all miss it. The title points to the signal an integrated trailer brake controller uses to gauge how hard the driver is braking.
s: Trailer brakes weak, delayed or not applied when the vehicle brakes
Trailer brake warning message in the instrument cluster
c: Open, shorted or corroded wiring or connector of the brake force or pressure signal
Brake pressure transducer or deceleration sensor defective
Trailer brake controller module faulty or wrongly configured
